title: Ultimate Chilli
method: Pulse mushrooms in a food processor until finely minced[cite: 4].
Heat a little olive oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat; cook minced mushrooms with ¼ tsp salt and ¼ tsp black pepper for 5 minutes, then set aside in a bowl[cite: 4].

Peel and mince red onions and garlic[cite: 4]. Deseed and finely chop the red chillies[cite: 4]. Pick coriander leaves and finely chop stalks[cite: 4]. Dice celery and red pepper into small chunks[cite: 4].
Heat olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat; cook minced onions, garlic, coriander stalks, and chillies for 5–10 minutes, stirring constantly[cite: 4]. Stir in celery and red pepper[cite: 4].
Add the spice mix (chilli powder, ground cumin, smoked paprika, ground cinnamon, dried oregano, ½ tsp salt, and ½ tsp black pepper) and tomato purée; stir to coat vegetables[cite: 4].
Pour in red wine, soy sauce, and balsamic vinegar[cite: 4]. Increase heat to high and stir constantly until liquid reduces by two-thirds and alcohol evaporates[cite: 4].
Tip chopped tomatoes into the pan, stir, and simmer for 5 minutes until noticeably thicker[cite: 4].
Drain black beans and kidney beans[cite: 4]. Add to the pan along with maple syrup, dark chocolate, cooked minced mushrooms, and bay leaf[cite: 4].
Reduce heat to a gentle simmer with lid off, stirring occasionally, for at least 10 minutes until thickened and rich[cite: 4].
Remove bay leaf, stir through coriander leaves, and serve[cite: 4].
